newsitem.title: INDIA: India holds off on sugar deregulation - Deve Gowda.
newsitem.headline: India holds off on sugar deregulation - Deve Gowda.

text.p: Indian Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda was quoted as saying the government was keen to deregulate the sugar industry but would first take into account the interests of farmers and cooperative sugar factories.
Deve Gowda's United Front coalition has pledged to delicense, or deregulate, the sugar industry as part of a broader liberalisation programme.
But the plan has come under fire from farmers and cooperative sugar factories, as well as some state governments.

"It is my commitment that the government will not betray the farmers, and any decision on the issue would be taken after taking into account the concerns of the farmers, the private sector and the cooperative movement," United News of India quoted Deve Gowda as saying on Saturday.
"We would like to examine in depth" the implications of deregulation, the Press Trust of India quoted Deve Gowda as saying.
